newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks reach all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks reach all-time high.

text.p: Australian stocks surged through the 2,700 barrier to a record high shortly after opening on Friday following a rebound on Wall Street and strong performances by resource and bank stocks the previous day.

At 10.10 a.m. (0010 GMT) the All Ordinaries Index was 11.1 points up from Thursday's record closing high to 2,704.4. Friday's new mark was also 9.4 points higher than the previous all-time high set during trading on Tuesday.
The Dow Jones Index on Thursday snapped a three-day run of dips to pick up 58.53 points and close on 7,777.06, prompting local brokers to predict the All Ordinaries would breach 2,700.
Brokers and dealers felt the local market could go even higher but added more rises in the short term were unlikely.

"I think the market in general can go a hell of a lot higher in time, but we've had a very good run and I would expect it to consolidate at some point," said Morgan Stockbroking equities adviser Tony Russell.
"The kick along was some overseas investment funds coming into our resource and major stocks on the back of our dollar, as well as further speculation on an interest rate," he said.
Blue chip miner BHP was again at the forefront of the latest surge, reaching A$20.05 in early trade, its highest point since May 8 last year.
At 10.50 a.m. (0050 GMT), BHP was up 16 cents to A$19.88 and the volume leader after 2.7 million shares were traded.

Nickel producer QNI Ltd was left behind in Friday's record run as shareholders revolted against its merger with South African miner Gencor Ltd. After dropping 15 cents early, QNI was down 12 cents at 11.10 a.m. (0110 GMT) to A$2.53.
Brokers said institutional investors in particular had decided the nickel assets contributed to the deal by Gencor were over-valued and that Gencor had received more favourable terms than QNI.
National Australia Bank led a strong banking sector and was up 11 cents at A$18.94.
